# Community communication channels {.unnumbered}

Bioconductor community members use several platforms for questions, discussion, and coordination. Choose the channel that best fits your needs.

## The bioc-devel mailing list

Created in [March 2004](https://github.com/r-mailing-lists/data), the bioc-devel mailing list is for package development and Bioconductor infrastructure questions, particularly when input from developers or the core team may be needed.

New users can subscribe to the mailing list at <https://stat.ethz.ch/mailman/listinfo/bioc-devel>.

## The Bioconductor support site

Launched in [August 2014](https://support.bioconductor.org/p/61060/), the Bioconductor support site is the best place for questions about using Bioconductor packages. Its archived, searchable answers can help future users with the same issue.

The support site is available at <https://support.bioconductor.org>, where new users can freely create an account to post questions and answers.

## The Bioconductor Zulip chat

Bioconductor uses [Zulip](https://zulip.com/), a freely accessible, open-source chat platform, for community discussion, brainstorming, coordination, introductions, announcements, mentoring, working groups, and event planning.

New users can sign up at <https://chat.bioconductor.org/>. See [Using the Bioconductor Zulip chat](using_the_zulip_chat.qmd) for an introduction to channels, topics, and getting started.
